text:
amanda: Quick RFC follow-up — we didn't land the service-token scoping bits in the spec. TL;DR: do we enforce project-scoped tokens everywhere (gateway + service), or allow org/global service principals with per-resource checks? RFC here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026-authz-patterns

kevin: I still prefer project-scoped tokens for most components. Easier to reason about blast radius. Global principals are convenient for infra but make RBAC messy.

eli: Agreed on blast radius. Two operational constraints: 1) perf — signature verification on hot path, 2) cross-project workflows (analytics, billing) need a way to act across projects without giving full org power.

sara: For cross-project, we could use short-lived impersonation tokens issued by an auth service with explicit delegate list. Eg flow: svc-a requests impersonation -> auth svc verifies permission -> returns token with 'imp' claim pointing to svc-a and 'aud' to project-b.

amanda: Sketch of JWT claim shape I had in mind:

```
{
  "iss": "auth.redwood", 
  "sub": "svc-orders",        # principal
  "aud": "project:billing",  # target project (or org:team)
  "scp": ["invoice:create","invoice:read"],
  "imp": "svc-analytics",    # optional impersonator
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

amanda: Enforcement model: quick checks at the edge/gateway: signature + aud + exp. Deeper RBAC (role -> perms mapping) at the service level where the resource lives. That keeps fast-fail at gateway but authoritative checks with full context at service.

kevin: Gateway cache note: we can't call introspect for every request. Two options: 1) verify JWT locally (HMAC/RSA) and cache verification result for token id until exp, 2) issue opaque tokens and use very fast introspect service with local caches. I prefer signed JWTs (option 1) for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private customers we need introspect option.

eli: Key rotation + revocation tradeoff: short TTL (<=5m) avoids most revocation ops. But we need immediate revoke for compromised keys. Proposal: short default TTL + revocation stream that updates gateway caches (pub/sub) for tokens/keys to drop early. If customer wants, we support introspect + KMS/EKM for on-prem.

sara: What about RBAC model? Role-based at project boundary is simplest: roles = {viewer, editor, admin, svc-invoke}. Map roles to scopes. Later we can add ABAC attributes (env, region) if needed.

kevin: One more perf detail: prefer HS256 (HMAC) for internal tokens signed by auth service nodes for speed, but we must support RSA/ECDSA for cross-service verification when services can't share HMAC secrets (Dedicated/private). Document both.

amanda: Ops question — auditing. All token issues, impersonations, and revocations must be emitted to audit-log stream with project id, actor, and reason. Keep tamper-evident retention for 90 days (hosted) or configurable for enterprise.

eli: Implementation plan (rough):
- MVP: JWTs for hosted, project-scoped, short TTL 5m, gateway does signature+aud checks, services enforce RBAC.
- Delegation: impersonation token endpoint with explicit allowlists; impersonation tokens also short TTL.
- Revocation: revocation pub/sub + gateway cache invalidation; fallback introspect for Dedicated.

sara: +1 to MVP. Need migration plan for existing global tokens — auto-map to org-level roles and create scoped tokens during rotation window.

amanda: Action items:
- kevin: draft token format + key rotation doc (due Wed)
- eli: prototype gateway cache invalidation (pub/sub pattern) and perf numbers (due Fri)
- sara: write RBAC role->scope mapping and migration steps (due Mon)

ops-bot: NOTE: deploy-bot will create a follow-up thread for the migration checklist when kevin lands the token-format doc.

amanda: Sounds good. If no objections I'll update the RFC with these decisions and call this thread the follow-up record. :thumbsup:

kevin: no objections.

eli: fine by me.

sara: ok.

amanda: Closing in ~24h unless new concerns.
